text: dsh-turn-budget 是用于 DeepSeek Harness 的每轮资源预算插件。它通过 agent/pre-step 和 tools/pre-execute 生命周期钩子限制每轮模型请求步数、工具执行次数，并按供应商报告的用量累计输入、缓存与输出 token。工具调用上限覆盖携带 Agent 的根调用和嵌套调用，超限时在执行前拒绝；步数或 token 达到上限时阻止下一次模型请求。默认配置提供每轮 24 步和 40 次工具调用，也可设置 token 上限。适合需要控制长时间 Agent 轮次资源消耗的 DSH 部署；至少要启用一项正整数限制，不需要额外账号或 API 密钥。

dsh-turn-budget limits per-turn model steps, tool calls, and provider-reported tokens in DeepSeek Harness. Lifecycle hooks deny excess tools before execution and stop requests at configured limits. Defaults allow 24 steps and 40 tool calls; enable at least one positive integer budget.

让超出预算的模型请求在发出前被拦下来。
嵌套工具调用也需要计入每轮调用额度，怎么配置？

I need to deny tool calls before execution once a turn quota is used up.
Can I stop the next model request when reported token usage reaches a per-turn limit?
dsh-turn-budget 的功能「每轮模型步数限制」：按当前模型请求步数检查 maxStepsPerTurn，超过上限时拒绝该步。通过 agent/pre-step 在请求前执行。
dsh-turn-budget 的功能「每轮工具调用限制」：统计当前 Agent 轮次已准入的根及嵌套工具调用；达到 maxToolCallsPerTurn 后，在工具主体执行前返回拒绝结果。
dsh-turn-budget 的功能「供应商 token 预算」：汇总当前轮次每一步最新的供应商用量记录，避免重复计算 chunk 与最终消息；达到 maxProviderTokensPerTurn 后拒绝下一次模型请求。
dsh-turn-budget 的功能「预算配置校验」：加载时要求至少启用一种预算，并确保配置值为正的安全整数；空配置或无效数值会抛出错误。

`dsh-turn-budget` is a fail-closed resource governor for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It limits model steps, root and nested tool executions, and exact provider-reported token usage independently for every Agent turn.

The plugin uses public Harness extension points only:

dsh-turn-budget README · dsh-turn-budget：- `agent/pre-step` rejects a model request that would exceed the step or provider-token ceiling.
- `tools/pre-execute` denies a tool body before dispatch when the turn has consumed its tool-call allowance.
- Existing `tool/result` and `turn/end` records preserve the resulting policy outcome in the canonical Session log.

dsh-turn-budget README · dsh-turn-budget：This is a circuit breaker, not a billing system. It does not estimate currency, rewrite tool arguments, replace sandboxing or approvals, or terminate an uncooperative model/tool operation in the middle of a step.

dsh-turn-budget README · Install from a checkout：```sh
git clone https://github.com/Nunchakus888/dsh-turn-budget.git
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-turn-budget
dsh --profile web --dump-config
dsh --profile web

The bundled profile layer enables a conservative baseline of 24 model steps and 40 tool executions per turn. Override the complete row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` when a deployment needs different ceilings:

```yaml
- update:
    id: turn-budget
    config:
      maxStepsPerTurn: 16
dsh-turn-budget README · Install from a checkout：Every configured limit must be a positive safe integer. At least one limit is required.

dsh-turn-budget README · Enforcement semantics：| Limit | Enforcement point | Counted work | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxStepsPerTurn` | Before the next model request | Entered requests in the current turn | The proposed step is rejected; the turn closes as `blocked`. |
| `maxToolCallsPerTurn` | Before each tool body | Root calls plus Code Mode/nested dispatches carrying the Agent | Excess calls return a policy error naming the exceeded budget; the model retains one opportunity to finish without another tool. |
| `maxProviderTokensPerTurn` | Before the next model request | Latest provider usage per step, including cache read/write buckets | The proposed step is rejected after the reported total reaches the ceiling. |

dsh-turn-budget README · Enforcement semantics：Token enforcement is exact only when the provider reports usage. Missing provider usage is not estimated. A provider can exceed the configured ceiling inside its current response; the plugin prevents the following request because the public lifecycle exposes no preemptive token stream budget.

The tool ledger is process-local and keyed by live Agent identity. Cold recovery closes interrupted turns before they can continue, so a process restart cannot resume an old in-flight ledger.

dsh-turn-budget README · Development：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run check
```

The integration tests boot the real Agent Loop with the published Harness testkit. They cover step rejection, pre-dispatch tool denial, per-turn reset, final-response allowance, provider-token accounting, and duplicate usage replacement.
